catalog_quote: Accent. — The data with regard to accent and emphasis are very meagre. De Morgan prints the strongly accented part of a word in clarendon and the rest in ordinary type, except " very short " syllables, which he prints in italics. Most collectors fail to mark the accentuated syllable, but it will often be found indicated by an acute accent (') in the spelling I have adopted. As a rule, the accent in all the aboriginal dialects appears to fall on the final syllable. This is most marked, however, in Sakai, where the final syllable is apparently the real root of the word, but the tendency is also traceable in Jakun, even in words of Malayan affinity. This is contrary to Malay usage, but, as in Achinese and Cham, is probably due to Mon-Khmer influence. ... new_statements.rule_in_words: Only a group-level, hedged 1906 remark: in the 'Jakun' (Aboriginal Malay) dialects, the group comprising Blandas/Belandas and Mantra (the historic Temuan) and Jakun of Johor, a tendency toward final-syllable accent is 'traceable', unlike Malay. No Temuan-specific modern source that could be opened states where word stress falls; the accessible modern descriptions (Looi, Baer & Mohamad 2018; Rohani & Noor Hasnoor 2014) are silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Blagden notes the accent data are 'very meagre' and that most collectors failed to mark accent; no lexical exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic word-level accent as marked in 19th-century collectors' wordlists (citation forms); not specific to Temuan and not a phonological analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Looi, Baer & Mohamad 2016/2018 describe the Temuan of central Selangor (Ulu Serendah, Ulu Kuang, Bukit Manchong, Sungai Kelubi, Sungai Tua, Ulu Rasau), noting marked dialect differences vs Hulu Langat and other states. Blagden 1906's remark is about the 'Jakun' group of Aboriginal-Malay dialects as a whole, i.e. Blandas/Belandas (Kuala Langat, Selangor) and Mantra/Mentera (Malacca), the historic names of the Temuan (temu1239), together with Jakun of Johor (jaku1239); it is not a Temuan-specific statement. The unpublished theses cover Temuan generally (Yunus 1968, Abdullah Hassan 1969), Hulu Langat (Rose Hanita 1991) and Melaka (Faredah Mahadi 1983-84).

sources.note: Blagden, Grammatical Notes p. 773 'Accent': data very meagre; as a rule accent in all the aboriginal dialects appears to fall on the final syllable, most marked in Sakai, 'the tendency is also traceable in Jakun, even in words of Malayan affinity', contrary to Malay usage. 'Jakun' here = Aboriginal-Malay dialects incl. Blandas (Selangor) and Mantra (Malacca), the historic Temuan, plus Jakun of Johor. Group-level, hedged, compiled from collectors' markings.
English article gives vowel/consonant tables (from Looi et al. 2018) with no stress information; Malay article is a stub.
